Festive Season Riding

The Christmas and New Year period offers unexpected riding opportunities. With time off work, quiet roads (especially Christmas Day itself), and the festive atmosphere of Britain's towns, a winter holiday ride can be surprisingly enjoyable.

Christmas Riding Traditions

  • Toy runs: Many motorcycle clubs organise Christmas toy runs in December — riders dressed in Santa outfits carrying presents for children's charities. Great fun and excellent community spirit.
  • Boxing Day ride-outs: A popular tradition. Clubs meet at a predetermined point on December 26th for a group ride. Check local motorcycle groups for details.
  • Christmas Day ride: For the truly dedicated. Christmas morning offers the emptiest roads of the entire year. A 20-mile loop before lunch on deserted roads has a magical quality.

New Year Riding

  • New Year's Day first ride: Starting the year on two wheels is a time-honoured tradition. Even a short ride around the block counts.
  • Resolution rides: Many riders use January 1st to commit to a year of riding goals — monthly mileage, a summer tour, visiting every national park.
  • Twixmas riding: The quiet days between Christmas and New Year (December 27-30) often offer surprisingly mild weather and empty roads.

Practical Considerations

  • Road conditions: Christmas weather can be anything from mild and dry to snow and ice. Check forecasts and don't ride if ice is likely.
  • Services: Many petrol stations, cafes, and shops close on Christmas Day and may have reduced hours over the holiday period. Plan your route around available services.
  • Breakdown cover: Verify your breakdown cover operates over the bank holidays. Recovery times may be longer than usual.
A Boxing Day ride with friends, finishing at a pub for a restorative pint and mince pies, is one of the year's finest motorcycle traditions. Wrap up warm, ride carefully, and enjoy the camaraderie of being out on two wheels when most people are on the sofa.

Winter Social Riding Events

The Christmas period is one of the most socially active times in the UK motorcycle calendar. Toy runs — where riders carry wrapped presents to children's hospitals and charitable organisations — happen in most regions during December. These organised events bring hundreds of riders together for a common cause in a genuinely festive atmosphere that warms the heart as much as the heated grips warm the hands.

Boxing Day meets at favourite pubs, cafés, and biker gathering points are well-established traditions in many regions across the country. Check local motorcycle forums and Facebook groups for events happening near you. New Year's Day gatherings at famous biker stops draw enthusiastic crowds regardless of weather conditions. The Ace Café in London, Squires Café in Yorkshire, and Matlock Bath in the Peak District all see significant numbers of riders on January 1st, creating an optimistic and forward-looking atmosphere that perfectly launches the riding year ahead.

If you prefer solitary riding, the quiet days between Christmas and New Year — often called Twixmas — frequently deliver surprisingly mild weather combined with completely deserted roads. Everyone else is at home digesting festive leftovers while you have the countryside entirely to yourself.

faq.q: Is it safe to ride over the Christmas period?
faq.a: It can be, but conditions dictate everything. Christmas weather ranges from mild and dry to snow and ice. If the temperature is below 3C, assume ice is possible, especially on bridges and shaded roads. Stick to gritted main roads, keep rides short, and if in doubt, do not ride.

faq.q: What is a Boxing Day ride-out?
faq.a: It is a popular tradition where clubs meet at a predetermined point on 26 December for a group ride, usually finishing at a pub for a restorative drink and mince pies. Check local motorcycle groups and Facebook pages for meeting points and times near you.

faq.q: Should I check breakdown cover over the holidays?
faq.a: Yes. Verify your breakdown cover operates over the bank holidays and be aware that recovery times may be longer than usual. Many petrol stations, cafes, and shops close on Christmas Day and run reduced hours across the period, so plan your route around services that will be open.

Twixmas is the quiet stretch from 27 to 30 December. It frequently delivers surprisingly mild weather and completely deserted roads while everyone else stays at home. If you prefer solitary riding, this is one of the best windows of the winter to have the countryside to yourself.
